subject: audiology
intro: Audiology leads into the clinical hearing professions: the audiologists who measure hearing and fit the technology, the speech-language pathologists they work alongside, and the faculty who train the next generation.

roles.title: Audiologists
roles.what: Assess and treat people with hearing and related disorders: run the diagnostic test battery, diagnose the type and degree of loss, fit hearing aids and provide auditory training and rehabilitation.
roles.where: Units 3 and 4 are the clinical core — pure-tone and speech audiometry, immittance, OAEs and ABR, and classifying conductive, sensorineural and mixed loss — with unit 5's hearing-aid fitting as the treatment arm.

roles.title: Speech-Language Pathologists
roles.what: Assess and treat people with speech, language, voice and fluency disorders, including the communication and swallowing problems that follow stroke, injury or illness.
roles.where: Unit 6's aural rehabilitation, counselling and communication strategies are the shared toolkit, and unit 2's balance assessment and unit 3's ABR testing are the differential work SLPs and audiologists hand to each other.

roles.title: Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the health specialties to students in medicine, therapy and allied-health programmes, combining classroom instruction with clinical supervision and, often, research.
roles.where: This course is the syllabus you would teach: hearing science and psychoacoustics, the vestibular system, the diagnostic battery, and the hearing-technology unit from the AuD curriculum's knowledge areas.
